SYNTHETIC – NOT A REAL PATIENT
Low back pain began on 05/29/2026.
The patient denies any red flags such as trauma, cancer, fever, weight loss, bladder or bowel symptoms, saddle anesthesia, or progressive neurologic deficit.
Exam: Tenderness over lumbar paraspinals, limited range of motion due to discomfort. Neurologic exam shows normal lower-extremity strength, reflexes, and sensation.
Assessment: Acute low back pain, likely muscular/lumbar strain.
Plan: Initiated NSAIDs today; advised activity modification; follow-up in 2 weeks.

SYNTHETIC – NOT A REAL PATIENT
Patient returns for physical therapy follow-up. She reports ongoing low back pain.
Exam: Similar lumbar tenderness, neurologic exam unchanged.
Assessment: Persistent low back pain despite conservative measures.
Plan: NSAIDs were started on 05/30/2026 and continued through 07/10/2026 with partial response. Physical therapy was started on 06/05/2026, consisted of 10 sessions, and ended on 07/10/2026 with no improvement. Consider obtaining lumbar MRI to further evaluate.

SYNTHETIC – NOT A REAL PATIENT
Patient follows up after completing physical therapy. She reports continued low back pain without improvement.
Exam: Unchanged lumbar tenderness, neurologic exam within normal limits.
Assessment: Chronic low back pain, failed conservative therapy.
Plan: NSAIDs were started on 05/30/2026 and continued through 07/10/2026 with partial response. Physical therapy was started on 06/05/2026, consisted of 10 sessions, and ended on 07/10/2026 with no improvement. Spine surgery referral is under consideration pending MRI findings.

SYNTHETIC – NOT A REAL PATIENT
Patient returns for follow-up after completing conservative therapy.
Exam: Stable.
Assessment: Chronic low back pain, unchanged.
Plan: Lumbar MRI ordered today. Spine surgery referral is under consideration pending MRI findings.
